      END IF

UNTIL swapped = FALSE
ms: Faulty line: FOR i FROM 1 TO 5 (1); when i = 5 the comparison accesses nums(6), which does not exist (1). Correction: FOR i FROM 1 TO 4 — n − 1 (1).

q: This linear search always reports "Not found", even when the target is present. Identify the error and write the corrected line. (3)

q: This bubble sort produces a **descending** list, but an ascending list was wanted. Identify the faulty line and write the correction. (3)

      END IF

q: A student modifies a linear search to count **how many times** a value appears. It gives the wrong count. Identify the error and write the corrected loop condition or structure. (3)

q: Write a **binary search** algorithm in pseudocode for the sorted 50-item list `ids`, searching for `target` and displaying "Found" or "Not found". (6)
ms: first and last initialised to 1 and 50, found to FALSE (1); loop while not found and first <= last (1); mid = (first + last) DIV 2 (1); equality check sets found TRUE (1); correct half discarded: first = mid + 1 when ids(mid) < target, last = mid - 1 otherwise (1); result displayed after the loop (1).
msCode:
SET first TO 1
SET last TO 50
SET found TO FALSE
WHILE (found = FALSE) AND (first <= last) DO
   SET mid TO (first + last) DIV 2
   IF ids(mid) = target THEN
      SET found TO TRUE
   ELSE IF ids(mid) < target THEN
      SET first TO mid + 1
   ELSE
      SET last TO mid - 1
   END IF
END WHILE
IF found = TRUE THEN
   SEND "Found" TO DISPLAY
ELSE
   SEND "Not found" TO DISPLAY
END IF

q: Write a **bubble sort** in pseudocode that sorts the 8-item list `scores` into ascending order and stops as soon as a pass makes no swaps. (5)
ms: Outer REPEAT…UNTIL with swapped flag reset FALSE each pass (1); inner FOR i FROM 1 TO 7 (1); adjacent comparison scores(i) > scores(i + 1) (1); three-line temp swap (1); swapped set TRUE on swap and UNTIL swapped = FALSE (1).
msCode:
REPEAT
   SET swapped TO FALSE
   FOR i FROM 1 TO 7 DO
      IF scores(i) > scores(i + 1) THEN
         SET temp TO scores(i)
         SET scores(i) TO scores(i + 1)
         SET scores(i + 1) TO temp
         SET swapped TO TRUE
      END IF
   END FOR
UNTIL swapped = FALSE

q:

q:

Plan B still needs the full sort — thousands of comparisons — before its ≈10-comparison search (1), so the sort's cost cannot be repaid by a single search (1). q:
A vet's surgery keeps an unsorted list of 12 pet names entered during the day. At closing time the program must: sort the names into alphabetical order using a bubble sort, then let the vet type a name and be told "Seen today" or "Not seen", using a search suited to the sorted list.

Write the full algorithm in pseudocode. (6)
ms: Bubble sort: REPEAT/swapped structure with FOR i 1 to 11 (1); correct adjacent comparison and temp swap of names (1); sort stops on a swap-free pass (1). Search: name received, then a binary search with first/last/mid = (first + last) DIV 2 (1); halves discarded correctly using alphabetical comparison (1); "Seen today" / "Not seen" displayed from the found flag (1).
msCode:
REPEAT
   SET swapped TO FALSE
   FOR i FROM 1 TO 11 DO
      IF names(i) > names(i + 1) THEN
         SET temp TO names(i)
         SET names(i) TO names(i + 1)
         SET names(i + 1) TO temp
         SET swapped TO TRUE
      END IF
   END FOR
UNTIL swapped = FALSE

RECEIVE target FROM KEYBOARD
SET first TO 1
SET last TO 12
SET found TO FALSE
WHILE (found = FALSE) AND (first <= last) DO
   SET mid TO (first + last) DIV 2
   IF names(mid) = target THEN
      SET found TO TRUE
   ELSE IF names(mid) < target THEN
      SET first TO mid + 1
   ELSE
      SET last TO mid - 1
   END IF
END WHILE
IF found = TRUE THEN
   SEND "Seen today" TO DISPLAY
ELSE
   SEND "Not seen" TO DISPLAY
END IF
